problem: The chapter says that on 0 < x < L, 'sine times cosine integrates to 0'. That is false. Sine and cosine modes are mutually orthogonal only over a full period −L < x < L. On the half interval the cross integral does not vanish in general: for L = 1, m = 1, n = 2, ∫₀¹ sin(πx)cos(2πx)dx = −2/(3π) ≠ 0. A student who believes this would think a mixed sine–cosine series can be handled by the same one-mode-at-a-time rule.
fix: Say only what is true: 'Each family is orthogonal on 0<x<L: ∫₀^L sin(mπx/L)sin(nπx/L)dx = L/2 when m=n and 0 otherwise, and the cosine family obeys the same rule. Sine and cosine together are orthogonal only on the full period −L<x<L, not on 0<x<L, so do not mix the two families on a half interval.'
